name: Macromastia and Polymastia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Excess Breast Volume or Number

criteria.description: Presence of excessive breast tissue volume exceeding normal anatomical limits
Identification of one or more accessory breasts or nipples along the embryonic milk line
Symptoms such as back pain, shoulder grooving, or skin irritation attributable to excess breast tissue

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of breast hypertrophy or supernumerary breast tissue confirmed by clinical examination
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; imaging may assist in delineating extent of tissue

pathognomonic.symptomName: Marked breast hypertrophy exceeding normative size parameters
searchTerms: very large breasts beyond normal size

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of supernumerary nipples or breast tissue along milk line
searchTerms: extra nipples or breast tissue along milk line

common.symptomName: Chronic interscapular and cervical spine pain due to breast weight
searchTerms: chronic upper back and neck pain from large breasts
pain between shoulder blades due to breast weight
cervical spine pain from heavy breasts

common.symptomName: Skin maceration or intertrigo beneath breast folds
Psychological distress related to body image
searchTerms: mental health concerns about body shape

occasional.symptomName: Postural abnormalities secondary to breast weight
searchTerms: posture problems caused by heavy breasts
spinal alignment issues from breast weight

occasional.symptomName: Nipple discharge from accessory breast tissue
searchTerms: nipple fluid from extra breast tissue

occasional.symptomName: Localized skin ulceration beneath large breast folds

searchTerms: localized limb swelling due to lymph blockage

rare.symptomName: Malignant transformation within accessory breast tissue
Neuropathic pain due to nerve compression

imaging: Ultrasound demonstrating excess glandular and fatty breast tissue
MRI delineating extent of accessory breast tissue
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; possible familial aggregation in some cases
other: Physical examination revealing hypertrophic breast tissue or supernumerary nipples

distinguishingFeatures: Extreme breast enlargement often during pregnancy or puberty
Rapid progression and possible systemic symptoms
Localized fatty tumor within breast tissue

redFlags: Skin changes suggestive of malignancy (ulceration, peau d’orange)
references: Orphanet: Excess breast volume or number - ORPHA:180170
American Society of Plastic Surgeons Clinical Practice Guidelines on Macromastia
UpToDate: Evaluation and management of breast hypertrophy
